newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mostly up on rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mostly up on rebound.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Wednesday on a technical rebound after two days of losses early in the week, traders said.
The most actively traded November 1997 contract closed at an intraday high of 3,331 yuan ($402) per tonne, up 41 yuan from Tuesday's close. It opened higher at 3,330 yuan and hit a low of 3,320 yuan.
July fell 80 yuan to 3,210 yuan per tonne, September rose 40 to 3,336, the January 1998 contract added four yuan to 3,289 and March gained 85 to 3,215 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 12,300 tonnes from 19,700 tonnes.
"Shorts were seen offsetting their positions to cash in, but the reduced volume indicated the market was still weak," said one trader.
"If there is no new stimulus, upward potential will be limited," the trader said.
